content.thinking:
The pure-Python fallback takes 4.19s for the absolute worst case (2048 disjoint deep paths) — acceptable as a fallback. And it agrees with the C core on 60 random cases.

Now let me test the fallback path end-to-end (with the compiler unavailable) to make sure `run` still works: run with PATH cleared.

Also let me test adversarial regex patterns for the guard.

arguments.command:
cd /app/tmp && cat > /app/tmp/test_nofallback.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Run the executable with an empty PATH so no C compiler can be found.
env -i PATH=/nonexistent /app/submit/run << 'INPUT'
{"op":"compile","fib":[{"prefix":"::/0","hop":7},{"prefix":"2001:db8::/32","hop":8},{"prefix":"2001:db8::1/128","hop":9}],"capacities":[4096,4096,4096,4096],"max_stride":32}
{"op":"compile","fib":[],"capacities":[4096,4096,4096,4096],"max_stride":32}
INPUT
EOF
chmod +x /app/tmp/test_nofallback.sh
time sh /app/tmp/test_nofallback.sh | python3 -c "
import sys, json
for l in sys.stdin:
    r = json.loads(l)
    print(r['status'], r.get('cuts'), r.get('peak'))
"
